title: After playing a bit of Lego Skylines, it seems like a city builder for people who care less about traffic jams and more about decorating
summary: A short preview revealed a cozy and calm builder with some gorgeous views.
body: It makes so much sense I can't believe it didn't happen years ago: as revealed at Gamescom last week, Lego is finally fulfilling its destiny by making a city builder . And I'm happy to say I got my eager hands on an early build of Lego Skylines for a little preview. I do want to make this clear: the preview build I played was very short, with only about 35 minutes of playtime. It was almost entirely focused on building one small neighborhood, with the population maxing out at around 50 residents by the end of the preview. That's not quite long enough, or big enough, to get a real feel for a city builder. But what's here is immediately appealing. The little Lego world I worked on was simply lovely. Click to build a house and it'll quickly be constructed in a colorful shower of Lego bricks falling from the sky and piling up into a cozy-looking little home. Bulldoze a mistake and the building will collapse into a heap of plastic bricks on the ground. The cute animations and cheery visuals are exactly what I'd hoped for when I saw the game's trailer last week, and again made me wonder why Lego didn't make a city builder years ago. title: 30,000 games are either Steam Deck verified or at least 'playable' on Valve's handheld
summary: Hands on, and on the go.
body: Valve's handheld launched in February 2022, opening the door to playing your Steam library on the go. Now, almost half a decade later, 30,000 games either enjoy the green stamp of being Steam Deck verified, or are at least considered 'playable.' According to the latest numbers from SteamDB that breaks down to 8,964 Steam Deck Verified games and 21,083 games considered 'playable' on the handheld (via Gaming On Linux ). That's a big jump from the 3,000 games either Verified or Playable back in May 2022 . 'Verified' means your game of choice should work great on the Steam Deck from first boot, whereas 'Playable' games require either some finagling or adjustments for the best experience. Steam Deck verification is also joined by similar compatibility checks for the Steam Machine , the soon-to-be-released Steam Frame , and SteamOS more broadly. I make the whole thing sound straightforward, but it's worth noting that the Steam Deck's full verification criteria can present developers with confusing hoops to jump through . One more thing to note: a game with neither badge doesn't necessarily mean it won't run on the Steam Deck at all. For just one example, Dragon Age: Origins is officiall…

summary: Rebel Wolves' vampire RPG is holding an aggregate 83 score on Metacritic.
body: The Blood of Dawnwalker isn't out until tomorrow—September 2—but the reviews are up now, and generally speaking they're pretty good. We gave it an 83% score in our review , calling it "a resolutely miserable horror RPG with some great ideas," and that lines up spot-on with its enviable 83/100 aggregate rating on Metacritic . title: GTA 6's story is too important for Rockstar to let you swap between Lucia and Jason whenever you want
summary: Outside of the story, however, you'll be free to swap whenever.
body: The recent GTA 6 "extended look" on Netflix wasn't very clear on whether you can swap between its protagonists Jason and Lucia at will. Apart from a moment where the camera pulls away from Lucia and back down to Jason miles away, there wasn't a lot of swapping going on, especially during the action. According to an interview on Famitsu with Rockstar North's co-studio head Rob Nelson (translated by GamesRadar+ ), the ability to swap characters will depend on the mission and where you're at in the story. "During the story, there are times where you can't switch from one character for some reason," he said. "There are some missions where you are free to switch as much as you want, but there are some sections where we want you to experience it from a certain character's perspective, like GTA 5, so we limit switching." As an example, Nelson said you used to be able to swap between Jason and Lucia during a mission early on in the game, but the team decided it would make more sense for Jason to take the lead with his military background. Other missions, like the one we saw in the extended look where the two are escaping a bank robbery, will do the swapping for you. After firing at the co…

title: August was a milestone month if you love watching robots completely eat it
summary: The World Robot Humanoid Games gave us more footage of malfunctioning robots than we know what to do with.
body: Here at Clanker Watch we're keeping a vigilant eye on the future as we uneasily enter the Age of Robotics. And there's never been a month like August of 2026 to keep that eye occupied with videos of robots breaking down, messing up, and in a few cases, straight-up catching on fire. That's due to the World Robot Humanoid Games in Beijing, a yearly event where robots compete in sporting events like running, boxing, jumping, weight-lifting, and even the tug of war. As we've seen in previous months, robots are prone to falling over and freaking out when they're doing stuff like moonwalking or, you know, standing perfectly still . Getting robots to race at speeds faster than Usain Bolt? There are gonna be some catastrophic fails. Let's look at our favorite robot moments from August. 1. Failympics There's no better place to start than with this highlight reel of fails from the World Robot Humanoid Games compiled by news.com.au . It's four glorious minutes of robots keeling over, smashing into each other, falling to pieces, shuddering, juddering, tripping, malfunctioning, sparking, burning, charging into walls, falling over tables, and being carted away on stretchers. title: This video of a power supply blowing up shows why you should never cheap out on your PSU
summary: New fear unlocked.
body: PSU fails dramatically from r/pcmasterrace It's accepted wisdom at this point that there are some things you probably shouldn't cheap out on: Tires, tattoos and medical devices sit among the top. But I say a good PSU should be up there if you want your rig to stay intact, as you definitely don't want it blowing up while attached to all of your pretty components. And a recent video going around Reddit has made me doubly sure of that fact. As shared to the PCMR subreddit , a tech worker was testing a PSU for a potential RMA for a customer. They plugged it in, and within a second, the entire back of it blew up, causing a fire. The sound it makes as it does so is truly horrible, with multiple components frying. At least, with video footage, they show why the RMA is justified. The employee luckily stepped away very quickly and appears to have avoided any harm. The PSU in question is a VSP Megamax, and judging from the picture showing off the aftermath , it's a 750 W model. That all occurred, of course, quite a few years ago now. title: Afterworld, Paradox's post-apocalyptic grand strategy game, let me conquer Florida with a band of alcoholic mutant cannibals
summary: And everyone seemed happy with the change.
body: With Afterworld , Paradox Development Studio is giving the post-apocalypse the Stellaris treatment, turning the end times into a ludicrously elaborate sandbox where you can live out all sorts of apocalyptic fantasies—whether you want to create a freewheeling band of road warriors or a new American empire. I went to Sweden to play an alpha build of this ambitious behemoth last month, and I've been able to keep playing at home since then. But this is a Paradox game, so I still feel like I'm barely scraping its dusty, radioactive surface. Here's a bit of what I've been getting up to, across multiple playthroughs: I made a band of alcoholic mutant cannibals, stole some bikes, and conquered Florida. I embraced the religion of the highway, creating a tribe of zealous petrol heads spreading their beliefs across the wasteland. I teamed up with an ancient immortal to help rebuild America, betrayed him, and tore the continent apart with our brutal civil war. I created a docile empire of slaves by making everyone addicted to drugs. I became a cheese magnate. Even in this alpha build, with its single origin and only one major threat, there's plenty to do—enough to give this would-be conqueror…

title: I've spent four months testing control pads in Counter-Strike and I've finally settled on my fave
summary: Tactical FPS players will want to check this out.
body: Most gamers enjoy a speedy or balanced feel to their mouse pad, but there are a few of us out there who have a penchant for stopping power. If you're into tactical shooters that require very steady aim plus occasional flicks with a precise stop on your enemy's head, slower control pads are for you. I've been trying out some different control pads in Counter-Strike 2 for months now and I feel like I'm finally able to draw some solid conclusions over which are best. At least as far as my own fingertips are concerned. Your mileage may of course vary. Personal favourite: Zowie H-SR III Noteworthy: Wallhack CR-005 Key terms Stopping power: How easy it is to stop your mouse where and when you want it to, presumably over an enemy's head. Static friction: How hard it is to get the mouse moving from stationary. The combination of this and dynamic friction makes for good stopping power. Dynamic friction: How hard it is to keep the mouse moving when in motion. The combination of this and static friction makes for good stopping power. Softer pads: Tend to be slower. body: As is the case with a lot of older games (I regret to inform you that The Witcher 3 is 11 years old) that get the remaster treatment, there's been some anxiety over whether The Witcher 3 Remastered will run properly on the Steam Deck—especially given it'll be a free update . It's always frustrating when some new glossy graphics pack messes with your hardware. Well, fear not—speaking to PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens ahead of Gamescom 2026 , CD Projekt Red's executive producer of external projects Jakub Kutrzuba has told us that The Witcher 3 Remastered will run just as well on your Steam Deck, thanks to general optimisation improvements with the new rendering engine. "When it comes to Steam Deck, based on what we see, the game will work the same way, but look much much better. body: I think it's fair to say that DLSS 5 is the most controversial Nvidia creation… well, ever. As the lights went down, it became obvious as to why. Here was the latest version of DLSS 5 running in front of us, the controversial graphics tech in the flesh. And the message Nvidia wanted to get across was deliberate, and strongly put: It's all about developer control. title: Fable system requirements seem reasonable but with a 30 fps target and no mention of upscaling it's hard to say for sure
summary: And you may want to make some on your SSD too.
body: With Fable (it's just called Fable, but it's technically Fable 4) set to release on February 23 next year, we finally have its system requirements. And for a big budget game launching in 2027, they're not too bad. That's according to the newly updated Fable FAQ , which says you will need an Intel i7 6850K or an AMD Ryzen 5 2600, paired with either an RTX 5050 / RTX 2060 , a Radeon RX 6600 , or an Intel A580 to run the game on a minimum. Minimum in this case means running the game at 1080p at 30 fps. With the RTX 2060 being a budget-to-mid-range graphics card from 2019, and both suggested CPUs being nearly a decade old, these are reasonably unintensive requirements, assuming you can stomach 30 fps. Especially for what looks to be a very good-looking game . The recommended specs ( which in this case means running the game on Medium ) are an Intel i5 11600KF or AMD Ryzen 5 5600 paired with an RTX 5060 / RTX 3060 TI , or an AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT / RX 7600 XT . There's no Intel GPU mention on this one, and 'recommended' entails playing the game on 1440p at 30 fps or at 1200p at 60 fps. title: One of Elden Ring's top sleuths has already unmasked its new DLC characters
summary: You look familiar.
body: Longtime FromSoftware dataminer Zullie the Witch has come out with a new video showing off the close-up details of Elden Ring's two new NPC invaders. Knight Leontiel and Noble Broken Mask were both added to the game as part of Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition DLC. Knight Leontiel is a straight "hey, I know them" reference to Lucatiel of Mirrah from Dark Souls 2, boasting an HD remaster of her signature conquistador fit and nimble greatsword. Take off the mask, though, and Leontiel practically is Lucatiel, even down to a burn mark over her left eye that corresponds to the hollowing rot Lucatiel suffered in Dark Souls 2. Noble Broken Mask, meanwhile, may obliquely give us a better idea of what his base game counterpart and spiritual rival, Goldmask, is supposed to look like. Goldmask's model has a face, but it seems like a generic placeholder element. Broken Mask has an austere, pinched face with striking pale gold eyes, and Zullie points out that he bears a more than passing resemblance to the typically obscured faces of Elden Ring's perfumer enemies. title: After the debacle of Cyberpunk 2077, CD Projekt says The Witcher 4 is already running on PC and consoles, promises 'it's going to run' on all target platforms
summary: Sure, it's a low bar, but after the Cyberpunk 2077 fiasco you can understand why CD Projekt Red would want to make the point.
body: Cyberpunk 2077 now is one of the best RPGs money can buy. But Cyberpunk 2077 then , which is to say when it was new, was not. It was pretty okay on PC , aside from a horde of bugs, but it was such a performance catastrophe on the PlayStation 4 that Sony literally booted it off the PlayStation Store . Even when it was allowed back in the building six months later, Sony slapped a notice on it warning people that it was still potentially dodgy . Speaking to Game Developer , CD Projekt Red co-CEO Michał Nowakowski said that failure arose from the studio's ambitions for the game, which led it to develop on PC first. "We want[ed] to push the boundaries of what is doable in terms of cinematic feeling and whatnot [in Cyberpunk 2077], and PC was just the best suited rig for that," Nowakowski said. "There was this, as it turned out, false belief that toning it down to whatever was the current gen is not going to be that much of a challenge." There was also a little bit of belief in a Polish take on the ol' Bioware magic : Nowakowski said the studio "got a bit lucky here and there" with The Witcher 3, leading it to believe that Cyberpunk would ultimately be fine too. title: I added player-seeking hit squads to GTA 5, though the billion other mods I have installed keep getting in their way

body: It is high time I paid for my crimes. There are things I've done that can't be forgiven, mostly relating to that time I drove a Chinese anti-air missile truck into Beverly Hills, and someone should make me face consequences for that. Alas, in GTA 5 , no one will unless I make them. So I made them. I have installed Ambient Hit Squads , a mod inspired by Red Dead Redemption 2 that will dispatch armed men to eliminate you every so often as you're out exploring the game's world. This functions more or less as it should in my nightmare-frankenstein version of GTA, already lumbering under so many mods. Once in a while, my map will bloom with red dots as armed assassins arrive to kill me, and the clatter of gunfire will join the now-constant chorus of cars ramming each other, pedestrians, geometry, me, and themselves. But of course, these hitmen have to navigate this reality too. For the guys who are just there —just men on the ground running at me, that's not so much of a problem. For the ones in helicopters, it is an irresolvable problem.
